title: Teaching
text: I teach the computing and analytics sequence in the Division of Business Administration — students arrive with no programming background and leave able to pull data, model it, and defend what the model says. All three courses are taught in a computer lab, and every session is built around code that students run themselves.

title: Teaching
text:
Advising
I supervise undergraduate research in AI policy, applied machine learning, blockchain and on-chain data analysis, and empirical finance. The projects I enjoy most start from a dataset nobody has looked at carefully yet — a public ledger, a permit filing, an administrative record — and ask what it can be made to reveal.
If you would like to work with me, send a short note describing the question you want to answer and any coursework or tools you have already picked up. Prior programming experience helps but is not a prerequisite; curiosity about where the data came from matters more.

title: Research
text:
My research runs along two tracks that keep meeting. One builds machine learning methods for problems where the data resist standard tools — sparse labels on a blockchain graph, free text in a permit filing, an agent population with no ground truth. The other uses those methods, and conventional econometrics, to ask who bears risk when a market or a policy shifts.
Working papers are listed with their current review status. Drafts are available on request; email me and I will send the most recent version.

title: Hojun Kang
text:
About
I am an Assistant Professor in the Division of Business Administration at Dongduk Women’s University. Three questions organise my work: how AI systems should be governed, how far they can be trusted as instruments of measurement and simulation, and what the digital records they produce reveal about risk in financial and housing markets.
Much of what I do begins with a record that was never meant for research — a blockchain ledger, a municipal permit filing, a mortgage application file — and asks what can be credibly recovered from it. That commitment runs in both directions: machine learning lets me read sources that were previously unreadable at scale, and the same scrutiny I apply to an administrative record I apply to the models themselves, asking where their answers stop being trustworthy.
Before joining Dongduk, I was a Senior Researcher in the AI Policy Research Division of the Software Policy & Research Institute (SPRI), where I led analysis of AI regulatory trends, impact assessment of high-impact AI systems, and measurement of the AI industry. I hold a Ph.D. in Management Information Systems from Sogang University.

title: Hojun Kang
text:
Research interests


AI policy and governance How regulators should assess the impact of high-impact AI systems, and how an AI industry that resists conventional classification can be measured at all.


LLM agents for economic and social science When an LLM-agent testbed can be trusted to answer a mechanism-design question, and how language models can read administrative text into research-grade measures.


Graph learning for financial security Graph neural networks and Transformer architectures that detect fraud and phishing on blockchain transaction networks, under the label scarcity and extreme imbalance that real deployments face.


Machine learning in finance and real estate Deep learning for asset valuation, and machine reading of public records to measure liquidity, displacement, and credit access in housing markets.
